A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LogicPro study. Text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, ablations, scaling experiments and dataset-difficulty measurements in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including main evaluations, analysis experiments and detailed appendix results in Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The same three-stage pipeline constructs reasoning problems, executes instrumented Python solutions and generates reasoning from intermediate variables. Consistency, solvability and execution checks, together with the appendix prompts, are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same LeetCode source problems, OpenHermes-2.5 and LogiCoT base data, and ten evaluation benchmarks listed in Section 3.1 and Table 6. No task or domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RuleTakers, LogicNLI, ProofWriter, CLUTRR, RuleBert, LogicBench and FLD. Base-data controls, source-code comparisons and mixed-baseline comparisons also retain identical membership.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same model configurations, training mixtures, three-epoch training settings, greedy decoding and Qwen-2.5-72B evaluation. Scaling procedures and the 5K-per-dataset difficulty evaluation in Section 4 are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same problem-conversion and intermediate-variable ablations, combined-baseline analysis, three scaling analyses, difficulty comparison, BBH subtask breakdown and two worked examples. Relocated displays introduce no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and aggregate scores without experimental seed counts, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding entries in Tables 1–9, plotted results in Figures 6–7 and example outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains LogicPro BBH scores of 50.9 for Qwen2-7B and 45.0 for Llama3-8B.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces a formal theoretical contribution. Mathematical reasoning within the algorithm examples, including the staircase recurrence and its derivation, is identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: program-guided synthesis of 540K examples from 2,360 algorithm problems, difficult and scalable reasoning data, and improved performance across reasoning benchmarks.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations for FOLIO performance, large-model gains and scaling bottlenecks. Limitations continue to emphasize better test-case generation and broader algorithm-problem sources, without new qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, the 32-A100 hardware disclosure, code/data availability statement and complete prompts in Figures 8–14 are unchanged. Appendix renumbering introduces no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2025), Revisit self-debugging with self-generated tests for code generation, in Section 5.1 and the references. Otherwise, research positioning and related-work coverage are retained from v2 Appendix A.

P1.justification: Related work moves from v2 Appendix A to v3 Section 5, renumbering the conclusion and remaining appendices. The author and affiliation block changes, acknowledgments are added, and limited editorial corrections appear; most prose is retained.

P2.justification: The same nine tables and sixteen figures remain, with changed spacing and placement. Figure 6 moves from page 7 to page 8, Table 9 from page 14 to page 15, and appendix prompts are redistributed without changing their contents.

improvement.justification: v3 brings existing related work into the main text and adds one background citation and acknowledgments. These limited organizational and editorial edits leave the explanations, empirical support, limitations and reproducibility information effectively unchanged. The rearranged displays remain readable, with no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
